title: Kospi plunges 5% as Asian markets slide; Sensex edges higher on IT buying
dek: A tech sell-off on Wall Street and the Binance hack hit Asia on Friday morning. Indian shares held up, while Brent crude stayed above $116 a barrel.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Asian stock markets fell sharply on Friday morning. South Korea's Kospi dropped about 5% in early trade, triggering a "sidecar" curb on programme selling for the second time in 11 trading days. Taiwan's benchmark lost about 3%, Japan's Nikkei 225 fell about 2.6% and Shanghai slipped 0.8%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng and Australia's ASX 200 bucked the trend and rose.

The slide followed a weak session for US technology stocks. On Thursday the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.38% and the S&P 500 lost 0.3% after quarterly results from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel disappointed investors and revived doubts about high valuations. The suspected $6.3 billion hack at crypto exchange Binance added to the unease.

## India

Indian shares were more resilient. In early trade the Sensex was up 138.77 points at 74,289.81 and the Nifty 50 rose 38.95 points to 22,967.10, building on Thursday's strong session, when the Sensex gained 905 points (1.24%) and the Nifty closed at 22,936.75.

IT stocks led the gains, with Infosys, TCS, HCL Tech and Tech Mahindra higher. Trent jumped about 6% after reporting a 25% rise in September-quarter consolidated net profit to Rs 468 crore. Bharat Electronics, State Bank of India, UltraTech Cement and Tata Steel were among the laggards.

Foreign institutional investors sold shares worth Rs 943.60 crore on Thursday, according to exchange data.

## Oil

Brent crude traded around $116 a barrel, up more than 1%. Prices remain high because shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is still disrupted by the conflict involving Iran. Analysts warn that oil above $115 keeps pressure on inflation in import-dependent economies such as India.

Figures are from early trade and will move through the session.
